draft.title: Preventing injury
card: light activity done before exercise, such as jogging and dynamic stretches. It raises body temperature and blood flow to the muscles, which helps prepare them for harder work.
easy activity done after exercise, such as slow walking and gentle stretching. It lets the heart rate and breathing return towards normal gradually.
a planned return to activity after an injury. It restores strength, movement and function step by step, so the athlete does not return too early.
Warm-ups and cool-downs help reduce the risk of a first injury. Proper rehabilitation helps stop the same injury coming back.
draft.remember: Warm up and cool down to reduce injury risk. Rehabilitate properly so an injury does not return.

a.q: Which action is mainly aimed at stopping an old injury coming back?
opts: Jogging and doing dynamic stretches before a game
Warming the muscles with light activity first
a.why: Rehabilitation rebuilds strength and movement step by step after an injury, which helps stop it returning. Warm-ups and cool-downs mainly lower the risk of injury in general.
a.clue: Which one happens after an injury has already occurred?

b.q: Tom hurt his hamstring at football and feels better after a week. He wants to play full matches straight away. What is the best advice?
opts: Follow a gradual return plan to rebuild strength first
Play now, as feeling better means the muscle has healed
Skip the warm-up, as the muscle is already loose
Stop all activity until he is fully pain free for a year
b.why: Rehabilitation returns an athlete to play step by step, which helps stop the injury coming back. Feeling better does not mean the muscle has regained full strength. Stopping for a year is not part of proper rehabilitation.
b.clue: Feeling better is not the same as being ready.

b.best: Follow a gradual return plan to rebuild strength first
